PullRequest.Title: Add structured multilingual GPT Live approvals
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341879.

Stacked on #339150. The base branch is `agents/pr-338709-review-fixes`; only the structured multilingual approval commit is part of this PR.

## Summary

Adds an explicit GPT Live Responses-delegation path for safe multilingual approval and rejection replies.

- Adds `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceResponsesModel` as an explicit opt-in because Responses delegation adds normal Responses API usage to each delegated voice request.
- Configures one bounded `route_voice_input` function with `approve`, `reject`, and `route_transcript` decisions.
- Uses the model only to propose a typed decision. VS Code remains authoritative for the active session, exact request and pending occurrence, prompt type, staleness, duplicate calls, and dispatch result.
- Routes ordinary coding requests and question-form answers using the captured transcript rather than model-generated text.
- Returns the actual dispatch result as a `function_call_output` and continues the delegated response before GPT Live acknowledges the action.
- Preserves the existing client-delegation transcript router when the new setting is empty.

## Safety boundaries

- A typed approval or rejection is accepted only for the exact captured prompt occurrence and only while that approval remains current.
- Stale, replaced, malformed, duplicate, wrong-tool, and non-approval calls do not authorize anything.
- Raw transcript text and model commentary are never treated as authorization.
- The configured Responses model uses `tool_choice: auto` so it can produce a final acknowledgement after a function result; the live instructions still require delegation before claiming success.
- Qualified or ambiguous consent is instructed to use `route_transcript`, where the existing deterministic router asks for an explicit response instead of authorizing it.

## Testing

1. Configure an OpenAI live model in `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel`.
2. Configure an accessible OpenAI Responses model in `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceResponsesModel`.
3. Start GPT Live Voice Mode with a pending approval and answer in a non-English language, for example `sí`, `oui`, or `ja`.
4. Verify the exact pending occurrence receives the typed approval only after VS Code validates it.
5. Replace or resolve the prompt before the function call arrives and verify no action is dispatched.
6. Try qualified consent, malformed arguments, duplicate function events, a normal coding request, and a question-form answer.
7. Clear `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceResponsesModel`, reconnect Voice Mode, and verify the existing client-delegation transcript behavior remains unchanged.

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/voiceClient/voiceLiveInputRouter.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceClientService.test.ts` — 101 passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/common/agentsVoice.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/browser/agentsVoice.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/voiceClient/voiceLiveInputRouter.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceClientService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/voiceClient/voiceLiveInputRouter.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/voiceClient/voiceClientService.test.ts` — passed.
- `cd extensions/copilot && npm run typecheck` — passed.

- `cd extensions/copilot && npm run test:unit -- src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/gptLiveSession.spec.ts src/extension/byok/vscode-node/test/byokContribution.spec.ts` — 15 passed.
- Repository formatter verification for all nine changed TypeScript files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Live provider validation was not run locally because it requires an OpenAI account with access to both the configured GPT Live and Responses models. Protocol fixtures cover the documented `session.delegation.created`, nested `response.output_item.done`, `response.item.create`, and `response.create` flow.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed manifest event, awaited activation call, and ordinary dictation callers are directly traced. The only uncertainty is how often users invoke speech before onStartupFinished has already warmed Copilot, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: extension-host module loading, service construction, and activation IPC for the full Copilot extension
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once per window/profile while Copilot is still cold; it is added to every first editor, terminal, or chat dictation invocation that races startup, regardless of whether BYOK Voice Mode is configured. Warm invocations avoid it after activation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and a blocked speech-session critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Copilot did not subscribe to the generic onSpeech event, so SpeechService.getProvider() did not wait for Copilot activation when starting ordinary speech-to-text; Copilot's onStartupFinished activation remained outside this user-initiated speech path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Adding onSpeech makes the existing SpeechService.getProvider() await activation of the entire Copilot extension before it can select a speech provider and create any speech-to-text session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `"onSpeech"` activation event at line 85 newly includes Copilot in the pre-existing awaited generic speech activation fan-out.
Findings.Title: Avoid activating Copilot for every cold speech session
Findings.Impact: Starting editor dictation, terminal voice input, or regular chat dictation immediately after launch can now stall while Copilot activates, even when the user has not configured or requested GPT-Live BYOK.
Findings.Evidence: extensions/copilot/package.json now registers the full extension for onSpeech. In src/vs/workbench/contrib/speech/browser/speechService.ts:256, getProvider() synchronously awaits extensionService.activateByEvent('onSpeech') before selecting the provider; callers include editorDictation.ts:358, terminalVoice.ts:176, and voiceChatService.ts:147. The extension already has onStartupFinished, so this line specifically moves its cold activation onto the interactive speech path rather than merely ensuring eventual activation.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not subscribe the full Copilot extension to the generic onSpeech event. Use a provider-specific live-session activation path (or activate the configured Copilot provider only from createVoiceLiveSession) so ordinary STT can proceed without waiting for Copilot, while preserving early BYOK provider registration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold ordinary editor, terminal, or chat dictation after launch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SpeechService.getProvider awaits extensionService.activateByEvent('onSpeech') before selecting the STT provider, so all matching cold extension activations must complete before dictation can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate extensions registered for the generic onSpeech event in the extension host, including loading and initializing the full Copilot extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once while Copilot is cold for a window/profile; zero additional activation work after it is warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot was not in the onSpeech activation fan-out and its existing onStartupFinished activation was not imposed by this speech request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The activation promise is awaited before speech-provider selection, directly delaying the first speech session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold extension state and the number/cost of extensions subscribed to onSpeech; this PR adds one large extension to that serialized prerequisite.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Extension activation may perform internal work concurrently, but getProvider serially awaits aggregate onSpeech activation before proceeding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold Copilot activation pays module/service initialization; subsequent speech sessions reuse the activated extension. No negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added manifest event and awaited ordinary-STT call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The delay depends on machine speed and whether onStartupFinished won the race before the user invokes dictation; this uncertainty supports medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression because unrelated cold dictation now waits for Copilot activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting configured OpenAI BYOK GPT-Live Voice Mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The controller awaits availability, microphone capture, WebRTC offer/ICE gathering, extension-host session creation, OpenAI session exchange, and remote SDP installation before the live session is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate onSpeech extensions and call the Copilot voice-live provider across the main-thread/extension-host bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Availability and session creation each cross the bridge once per connect; extension activation is effective only while cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls are prerequisites for connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the OpenAI model list to verify configured live-model access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per Voice Mode connect preflight; the result is cached only long enough to avoid a duplicate check within the same connect attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The BYOK path did not exist; hosted voice did not make this OpenAI request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before microphone/WebRTC session setup is accepted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST SDP and session configuration to OpenAI /v1/live/sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per successful configured BYOK connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hosted voice used the existing hosted WebSocket path instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Returns the remote SDP required to establish WebRTC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configured model and one connection attempt; retries/restarts repeat the per-connect boundaries rather than fan out per session item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Availability, capture/offer creation, ICE gathering, and session POST are predominantly sequential; cancellation and a connect-generation gate retire stale attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Availability is reused between controller preflight and VoiceClientService.connect for the same attempt, then cleared; model and session requests are cold again on a later connection. No result is retained across disconnects.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider/network latency varies, but the new remote work is opt-in and intrinsic to the new BYOK workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: network work is bounded to one request of each type per opt-in connection, the duplicate preflight is coalesced, and cleanup/cancellation are wired.

Scenarios.Scenario: Handling each GPT-Live utterance and optional Responses delegation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input transcript capture is correlated with one retained target; a delegation either routes locally or waits for one structured Responses function call, client dispatch result, and response continuation before acknowledgement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: OpenAI live audio/transcript and optional Responses delegation over the established WebRTC/data-channel session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delegation per user turn; Responses mode explicitly adds one model delegation per delegated turn, with parallel_tool_calls disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hosted voice used the existing backend WebSocket; client-delegation mode did not add normal Responses usage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Structured approval acknowledgement waits for the dispatch result and response continuation; ordinary local transcript routing avoids a separate client HTTP request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse incoming JSON events and serialize bounded data-channel result/append events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per transcript/event delta; append content is split into at most 500-byte chunks, while session thread/change payload producers cap items and text lengths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hosted WebSocket events were parsed once per backend message without this direct-provider adapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on the event-handler path, but realistic response and session-tool payloads are bounded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of turns and transcript deltas in a live session; retained captured inputs and response-delegation payloads are capped at 32. Two ID dedup sets last until disconnect, but their small per-turn entries did not establish a realistic user-visible regression at reviewed scale.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The delegated Responses tool configuration disables parallel tool calls; controller generation checks and per-request cancellation prevent stale dispatch from completing into a retired connection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No response cache; target snapshots and recent inputs are session-local, bounded by count, and cleared on disconnect. Duplicate call/delegation IDs are remembered for the session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-turn flow and retention lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long all-day sessions can accumulate small dedup ID sets, but evidence did not support material memory/GC impact sufficient for a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: expensive per-turn model use is explicit opt-in behavior, concurrent calls are constrained, and major payload-bearing collections are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Voice routing to a captured chat session, approval, question form, or session-information command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The controller validates the captured target and latest pending request, then sends through a resident widget or loads at most one target chat model before dispatch; session-information commands read and serialize in-memory session state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load one non-resident target chat session before sending or applying a response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one target-session load per routed turn; resident widget/model paths perform zero loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The response path already used acquireOrLoadSession; the diff adds shared cancellation and exact-target checks. Explicit send routing can select the same one-session load path rather than fan out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold target load is awaited before dispatch; cancellation aborts it when the voice connection is retired.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build JSON session summaries, changes, or up to ten capped conversation turns for voice model context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per explicit session-information tool call; visible sessions/files are capped at 20 and thread text at ten turns with per-field truncation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These shared voice tools existed; the diff adds an authoritative Agents-window delegate and direct-provider transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the requesting voice tool, off unrelated render/startup paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One captured session per turn; session-info collection scales across known sessions before sorting and then emits at most 20 entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each response uses one cancellation token and exact request; no collection-wide Promise.all or load burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resident chat models avoid loading; no new persistent cache is added. Cancellation and generation checks release cold references after stale attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for target cardinality and cancellation ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-list sorting can grow with unusually large histories, but calls are explicit and no changed boundary fan-out was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: changed routing remains one-target-at-a-time, bounded serializers are used, and existing cold loads are now cancellable.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 50 changed files and paginated large diffs. Reported the generic onSpeech activation regression. The new BYOK network path is opt-in and bounded per connection; per-turn delegation, serialization, target loading, and resource cleanup were traced without another high-confidence material regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
